text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.45% today to $457.22, continuing a five-day slide that has wiped out about 4% from its mid-October high. The decline comes despite crude oil prices hitting six-month highs—Brent crude topped $116 per barrel today—because geopolitical tension in the Middle East is creating uncertainty rather than stable refining margins. While high oil prices can help refiners' profits if they can buy crude cheaply and sell products at a premium, the risk of supply disruptions and potential U.S. military action against Iran is making the market jittery enough to keep buyers cautious on refinery stocks.

The timing matters: oil surged over the past two days on reports of U.S. plans to resume strikes on Iran, yet MPC kept falling even as crude climbed. This suggests investors are pricing in that geopolitical volatility—including the U.S. withdrawing diplomats from Saudi Arabia—outweighs the near-term benefit of elevated crude prices. Refineries are already running at a robust 93.4% capacity and fuel storage remains solid, so there's no supply tightness to drive refiner profits; the market is simply moving away from the sector while it watches the region.
